items.title: Why Cities Run Hot
items.text: On a summer afternoon, the center of a big city can be several degrees hotter than the countryside nearby. Scientists call this effect an urban heat island. Dark roads and roofs soak up sunlight, and concrete releases that heat slowly after sunset. Cities also have fewer trees, which normally cool the air by giving off water vapor. As a result, nights in the city stay warm, and people have a harder time sleeping. Some cities are now fighting the problem. Painting roofs white, for example, reflects sunlight instead of absorbing it. Planting trees along streets helps as well. These changes are not cheap; nevertheless, many planners believe the savings in air conditioning will eventually repay the cost.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "Concrete releases heat slowly after sunset. ______, nights in the city stay warm."
qs.why: 콘크리트가 열을 천천히 내보내는 것이 원인이고 밤에도 따뜻한 것이 결과이므로 As a result가 알맞아요.

qs.q: How does the sentence "Painting roofs white, for example, reflects sunlight..." relate to the sentence before it?
o: It names a cause of the heat island itself
It gives a specific way cities respond
It shows the problem is getting worse fast
It argues that roofs do not matter much
qs.why: 앞 문장의 '문제와 싸우는 방법'의 구체적인 예시를 들고 있어요.

qs.q: Which place would most likely be the coolest on a summer evening?
o: A park with many tall trees
A wide parking lot of dark pavement
A street lined with dark-roofed buildings
A plaza paved entirely with concrete
qs.why: 나무는 수증기를 내보내 공기를 식힌다고 했으므로 나무가 많은 공원이 가장 시원할 거예요.

qs.q: The phrase "soak up" in the passage is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: soak up sunlight는 햇빛을 흡수한다는 뜻이고 흰 지붕은 반대로 reflect(반사)한다고 했어요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why cities get hotter and what helps
How to design buildings that use less water
Why summer nights are longer in the countryside
How air conditioning has changed city life
qs.why: 도시가 주변보다 더운 이유와 해결책을 다루는 글이에요.

items.title: The Bus I Had to Take
items.text: I woke up late on the day of my big interview and ran to the station, but the train was already leaving. I felt like giving up. Instead, I checked the schedule and found that a slower bus would take me to the same town. It was not the plan I wanted; still, it was better than missing the interview altogether. On the bus, I reread my notes and calmed down. In fact, the long ride gave me more time to prepare than the train would have. I arrived ten minutes early, a little tired but ready. Looking back, I realize that the delay did not ruin my day. Rather, it taught me to stay flexible when things go wrong.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "It was not the plan I wanted; ______, it was better than missing the interview altogether."
qs.why: 원하던 계획은 아니었지만 그래도 낫다는 양보·대조 관계이므로 still이 알맞아요.

qs.q: What is the function of the sentence beginning "In fact, the long ride..."?
o: It admits that the bus was a mistake
It gives the reason the train left early
It describes how the interview ended
It adds a surprising supporting point
qs.why: In fact는 앞 내용(버스에서 안정을 찾음)을 뒷받침하는 놀라운 사실을 덧붙여요.

qs.q: Why most likely did the narrator feel calmer on the bus?
o: The bus was faster than the train would have been
The interview had been moved to a later time
A new plan worked and there was time to review
The narrator already knew every answer by heart
qs.why: 버스가 대안이 되었고 노트를 다시 볼 시간이 생겨서 마음이 가라앉았어요.

qs.q: The word "flexible" in the last sentence is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: stay flexible은 상황에 맞게 계획을 바꿀 수 있다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: How did the narrator get to the town?
o: By a taxi from the station
qs.why: a slower bus would take me to the same town이라고 했어요.

items.title: Stripes on the Savanna
items.text: Zebras are famous for their black and white stripes, but why they have them is still debated. One long-held idea was that stripes help zebras hide in tall grass. However, zebras live mostly on open plains, where stripes do little to hide them. A newer idea involves insects. Biting flies seem to avoid landing on striped surfaces. In one study, horses wearing striped coats were bitten far less often than horses in plain coats. This matters because flies spread illness among grazing animals. Therefore, many researchers now believe that stripes work mainly as protection from insects, although other benefits may exist as well. The question is not completely settled, but the evidence is growing.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "One idea was that stripes help zebras hide. ______, zebras live mostly on open plains, where stripes do little to hide them."
qs.why: 숨는다는 가설과 대비되는 사실이 이어지므로 However가 알맞아요.

qs.q: How does the sentence about horses in striped coats relate to the one before it?
o: It presents a view that opposes the claim
It offers evidence for the fly claim
It explains why zebras live on plains
qs.why: 파리가 줄무늬를 피한다는 주장의 증거로 연구 결과를 제시해요.

qs.q: What is the writer's attitude toward the insect explanation?
qs.why: many researchers now believe, other benefits may exist, not completely settled 등에서 신중하게 지지하는 태도를 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: The word "spot" in "easy to spot" is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: easy to spot은 눈에 띄기 쉽다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How lions hunt animals on the open plains
How horses are trained to wear striped coats
A new idea on why zebras have stripes
Why zebras travel together in large groups
qs.why: 줄무늬의 이유에 대한 오래된 가설과 새로운 가설을 다루고 있어요.

items.title: Home or Office?
items.text: Working from home has become common for office employees, and opinions about it are divided. Supporters point out that workers save time and money because they do not commute. Many also say they can concentrate better without office noise. Critics, on the other hand, worry that teams lose the casual conversations that spark new ideas. Younger employees, in particular, may miss chances to learn by watching experienced coworkers. For this reason, a number of companies now ask staff to come in two or three days a week. This mixed approach is not perfect, but it keeps some benefits of both. Whether it lasts will depend on whether managers can measure results fairly, not just hours spent at a desk.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "Supporters point to the time saved on commuting. ______, critics worry that teams lose casual conversations."
qs.why: 재택근무 찬성 측과 대비되는 비판 측 의견이므로 In contrast가 알맞아요.

qs.q: What does the sentence beginning "Younger employees, in particular..." do?
o: It narrows the worry to one group
It reverses the critics' main point
It lists a benefit that supporters claim
It describes a new company rule
qs.why: in particular는 앞의 걱정을 특정 집단(젊은 직원)으로 좁혀서 말해요.

qs.q: What does the writer imply about the two-or-three-day office schedule?
o: It is the best possible solution
It has failed in most companies
It is a compromise, not a perfect fix
It saves far more money than working at home
qs.why: not perfect, but keeps some benefits of both 라고 했으므로 절충안임을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: The word "spark" in the passage is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: spark new ideas는 새 아이디어를 불러일으킨다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: According to the passage, what do supporters of working from home say?
o: Younger staff learn faster from coworkers
People can focus better without noise
Managers can measure results more easily
qs.why: Many also say they can concentrate better without office noise라고 했어요.

items.title: Notice: East Lot Closure
items.text: NOTICE TO ALL STAFF. From Monday, June 3, the east parking lot will be closed for repaving. The work is expected to take two weeks. Therefore, employees who usually park there must use the west lot or the street spaces on Pine Road. Because the west lot is smaller, it will fill up quickly; for example, last month it was full by 8:30 a.m. Please arrive early or share rides with coworkers. In addition, bicycle racks will be moved next to the main entrance for the duration of the project. We apologize for any trouble. However, the new surface will be smoother, and the lines will be repainted, which should make parking easier afterward. Questions may be sent to the facilities desk.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "The east lot will be closed for two weeks. ______, employees who usually park there must use the west lot or Pine Road."
qs.why: 동쪽 주차장이 닫히는 것이 원인이고 다른 곳에 주차해야 하는 것이 결과이므로 Therefore가 알맞아요.

qs.q: Why does the writer mention that the west lot was full by 8:30 a.m. last month?
o: To explain why the east lot needs repaving
To announce a new start time for work
To compare it with the lot on Pine Road
To show that it fills up quickly
qs.why: for example로 서쪽 주차장이 빨리 찬다는 주장의 구체적 예를 들었어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about an employee who arrives at 9:00 a.m. during the closure?
o: The person may struggle to find a space
The person can use the bicycle racks as parking
The person will park in the repainted east lot
The person must work from home that day
qs.why: 서쪽 주차장은 8시 30분에 가득 찼으므로 9시에 오면 자리를 찾기 어려울 수 있어요.

qs.q: The phrase "for the duration of the project" means ______.
qs.why: duration은 지속 기간이므로 공사가 끝날 때까지라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why was this notice written?
o: To ask staff to pay for new parking
To prepare staff for a parking change
To invite staff to a cycling event
To report that a parking lot is complete
qs.why: 동쪽 주차장 공사로 인한 임시 변경을 직원에게 알리는 안내문이에요.

items.title: The Mystery of Yawning
items.text: Yawning seems simple, yet scientists still disagree about its purpose. For years, people believed that we yawn to take in extra oxygen. However, experiments showed that breathing more oxygen does not stop yawns. A different theory suggests that yawning cools the brain. When the brain becomes warm, a deep breath of cooler air may help lower its temperature. This could explain why people yawn more often when they are tired or bored, since the brain may run slightly warmer at those times. Yawning is also contagious: seeing someone yawn often makes us yawn too. Researchers think this may be linked to empathy. In other words, our bodies may react to the people around us without our noticing.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "People believed we yawn to take in oxygen. ______, experiments showed that breathing more oxygen does not stop yawns."
qs.why: 산소 가설과 실험 결과가 상반되므로 However가 알맞아요.

qs.q: What is the function of the last sentence, which begins with "In other words"?
o: It reports the result of a measurement
It restates the empathy idea simply
qs.why: In other words는 앞 내용을 쉽게 다시 말할 때 써요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the oxygen belief?
o: It has been proved by many experiments
It was widely held but is now doubted
It was never believed by ordinary people
It explains why yawns are contagious
qs.why: people believed ... However, experiments showed ... 라는 흐름에서 한때 널리 믿었으나 지금은 의심받는다는 것을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: The word "contagious" in the passage is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: contagious는 한 사람에게서 다른 사람에게 쉽게 옮는다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: According to the passage, when may the brain run slightly warmer?
o: When a person is tired or bored
When a person breathes extra oxygen
When a person is laughing with friends
When a person drinks cold water
qs.why: since the brain may run slightly warmer at those times 앞에 tired or bored라고 했어요.

items.title: Scan, Pay, Go
items.text: In many traditional markets, vendors who once accepted only cash now display a small square code beside their goods. Customers scan it with a phone and the payment is complete in seconds. For shoppers, the benefit is clear: there is no need to carry coins or wait for change. Vendors gain as well. They no longer worry about counterfeit bills, and their daily sales are recorded automatically. In addition, some banks offer small loans to sellers with a stable payment history. Still, the change is not easy for everyone. Older vendors may find the technology confusing, and a weak signal can stop a sale. As a result, many markets keep a few cash-only stalls and hold free classes to help sellers learn.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "Sales are recorded automatically. ______, some banks offer small loans to sellers with a stable payment history."
qs.why: 상인이 얻는 또 다른 이점을 덧붙이므로 In addition이 알맞아요.

qs.q: How does the sentence beginning "Still, the change is not easy..." relate to the earlier sentences?
o: It repeats the benefits in other words
It turns from benefits to difficulties
It gives an example of a benefit
It explains how the codes work
qs.why: Still 이후로 장점에서 어려움으로 화제가 바뀌어요.

qs.q: Why do many markets keep a few cash-only stalls?
o: Phones are not allowed near the stalls
Banks require markets to accept coins
Cash is always faster than a phone
Some sellers find the change hard
qs.why: 어려움을 겪는 상인이 있어서 현금 전용 가판을 일부 남긴다고 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: The word "stable" in the passage is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: stable payment history는 꾸준한 결제 기록을 뜻해요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How digital payment is changing traditional markets
Why cash will never be used again anywhere
How banks decide who receives loans
The history of coins and paper money
qs.why: 전통시장에서의 모바일 결제가 가져온 변화와 어려움을 다루는 글이에요.

items.title: Learning from Failure
items.text: We tend to admire successful inventors and forget how often they failed. One engineer, for example, built hundreds of prototypes of a small water filter before one finally worked. Each failure showed what to change next. Schools, however, often treat mistakes as something to avoid, so students may become afraid to try difficult tasks. Some teachers are therefore changing their approach. They praise effort and ask students to explain what went wrong, rather than simply marking answers incorrect. In addition, they let students revise their work for a better grade. Studies suggest that learners who see mistakes as information tend to keep trying longer. In short, failure is not the opposite of success; it is often part of the road to it.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "We forget how often inventors failed. One engineer, ______, built hundreds of prototypes of a small water filter."
qs.why: 실패를 많이 한 발명가의 구체적인 사례이므로 for example이 알맞아요.

qs.q: What is the function of the last sentence, which begins with "In short"?
o: It sums up the main message
qs.why: In short는 앞 내용을 요약하는 표현이에요.

qs.q: What would the writer most likely say about a student who revises a failed test?
o: The student should have avoided the test
The student is wasting time on old work
The student is learning from an error
The student is copying a classmate
qs.why: 실수를 정보로 보고 다시 시도하는 학습자를 긍정적으로 보는 글이에요.

qs.q: The word "prototypes" in the passage is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: prototype은 완성품이 나오기 전의 시험용 모델을 뜻해요.

qs.q: What do some teachers ask students to do?
qs.why: ask students to explain what went wrong이라고 했어요.

items.title: Paper or Screen?
items.text: Many students now read textbooks on tablets, but research suggests that the format matters. In several studies, readers who studied long texts on paper remembered main points better than those who read the same texts on screens. One explanation is that paper gives readers physical clues: they can feel how far they are through a book, which helps them build a mental map of the text. Screens, by contrast, scroll endlessly. Another problem is distraction. A tablet also holds games and messages, so attention is easily pulled away. This does not mean that digital reading is useless. Searching for a word or enlarging small print is far easier on a screen. The best choice therefore depends on the purpose of reading.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "With a book, readers feel how far they are. Screens, ______, scroll endlessly."
qs.why: 종이책과 화면을 대비하고 있으므로 by contrast가 알맞아요.

qs.q: What is the function of the sentence "This does not mean that digital reading is useless"?
o: It repeats the studies' main result
It softens the criticism of screens
It ends the discussion of paper
qs.why: 앞의 비판을 누그러뜨리고 화면 읽기의 장점으로 넘어가는 문장이에요.

qs.q: Which reader would the writer most likely advise to use paper?
o: A student preparing for an exam
A traveler looking up one unknown word
A reader who needs very large print
A person checking a bus time quickly
qs.why: 긴 글의 요점을 기억해야 하는 경우 종이가 낫다고 했어요.

qs.q: The word "enlarging" in the passage is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: enlarge는 크게 만든다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: According to the passage, why can a tablet cause distraction?
o: Its screen is much too small to read
It also holds games and messages
It costs more than a textbook
qs.why: A tablet also holds games and messages라고 했어요.

items.title: Power from the Tides
items.text: The moon's pull makes ocean tides rise and fall twice a day, and engineers want to use that movement to make electricity. Unlike wind or sunshine, tides are completely predictable, so power companies can plan exactly how much energy to expect. A tidal station works like an underwater windmill: moving water turns blades connected to a generator. The technology has drawbacks, though. Building in the sea is expensive, and salt water damages machinery quickly. Moreover, only coasts with strong tides are suitable. For these reasons, tidal power currently provides only a tiny share of the world's electricity. Nevertheless, supporters argue that it can work alongside solar and wind, filling the gaps when the sky is dark and the air is still.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "Building in the sea is expensive. ______, only coasts with strong tides are suitable."
qs.why: 또 하나의 단점을 덧붙이므로 Moreover가 알맞아요.

qs.q: How does the writer compare tides with wind and sunshine?
qs.why: Unlike wind or sunshine, tides are completely predictable이라고 했어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about solar power from the last sentence?
o: It cannot produce power at night
It is much cheaper than tidal power
qs.why: filling the gaps when the sky is dark라는 말에서 태양광은 어두울 때 전기를 만들지 못한다는 것을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: The word "drawbacks" in the passage is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: drawback은 단점을 뜻해요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How the moon moves around the Earth
Why wind power is better than solar power
How salt water is turned into drinking water
The strengths and limits of tidal power
qs.why: 조력 발전의 장점과 한계를 설명하는 글이에요.

items.title: The Bookshop That Stayed
items.text: Online stores can offer almost any book at a low price, so many small bookshops have closed. However, a few have survived by offering something a website cannot. One shop in a seaside town hosts weekly reading groups and invites local writers to talk about their work. Another sells used books alongside coffee, so customers stay and browse for hours. Staff also recommend titles based on conversations, whereas a website relies on a computer's guess. Of course, charm alone will not pay the rent. Owners therefore sell gift cards and run small online shops of their own. In this way, they are not rejecting technology but borrowing from it. Their experience shows that a business can compete without being the cheapest.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "Online stores sell books cheaply, so many small shops have closed. ______, a few have survived."
qs.why: 많은 서점이 문을 닫았다는 것과 대비되는 내용이므로 However가 알맞아요.

qs.q: How does the sentence about used books and coffee relate to the sentence before it?
o: It shows the result of closing a shop
It gives a second example of a special shop
It disagrees with the first example
It explains why books are so cheap online today
qs.why: 독서 모임 사례에 이어 또 다른 서점의 사례를 덧붙여요.

qs.q: What does the writer suggest about the shops that sell online?
o: They use technology to support their strengths
They plan to close their real stores soon
They have decided to close their real stores soon
They want to be the cheapest shops
qs.why: not rejecting technology but borrowing from it에서 기술을 활용해 자신들의 강점을 보완한다는 것을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: The word "browse" in the passage is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: browse는 가볍게 훑어보는 것을 뜻해요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why people prefer reading to watching videos
How a seaside town became famous for books
Which books sell best in used bookstores
qs.why: 온라인 서점과의 경쟁 속에서 동네 서점이 살아남는 방법을 다뤄요.

items.title: Review: The Clockmaker's Room
items.text: Our group of five tried this escape room last Saturday, and we had a mostly enjoyable time. The story is clever: you must find hidden gears before a giant clock stops. The puzzles are well designed. For example, one uses a mirror and a map in a way I had never seen. In addition, the staff were friendly and explained the rules clearly. However, the room was very dark, and a few clues were hard to read even with a flashlight. Because of this, we needed three hints and finished with only one minute left. I would still recommend it, but I would suggest bringing a stronger light. Overall, four stars out of five.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "The puzzles are well designed. ______, one uses a mirror and a map in a way I had never seen."
qs.why: 잘 설계된 퍼즐의 구체적 사례이므로 For example이 알맞아요.

qs.q: How does the sentence beginning "However" relate to the praise before it?
o: It gives another reason to praise the room
It repeats the rules in other words
It describes how the story ends
qs.why: However 이후로 칭찬과 대비되는 단점(어두움)을 말해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the group's result?
o: They almost ran out of time
They finished well before the deadline
They did not use any hints
They gave up near the end
qs.why: 세 번의 힌트가 필요했고 1분을 남기고 끝냈으므로 시간이 거의 부족했어요.

qs.q: The word "suggest" in the passage is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: I would suggest bringing a stronger light는 더 밝은 조명을 가져가라고 권한다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Which problem did the reviewer mention?
o: The staff explained the rules too fast
The story was too easy to follow
The room was too crowded with players
Some clues were hard to read
qs.why: a few clues were hard to read라고 했어요.

items.title: Farming on Fire Mountains
items.text: Living near an active volcano sounds dangerous, and it is. Yet millions of people farm the slopes of volcanoes around the world. The reason lies in the soil. When a volcano erupts, it throws out ash that contains minerals such as potassium and phosphorus. Over time, rain breaks the ash down and mixes it into the ground, making the soil unusually rich. Crops such as coffee, grapes, and rice often grow well on these slopes. Farmers therefore accept the risk in return for larger harvests. Nonetheless, the risk is real. Eruptions can bury fields in a single day. For that reason, many volcanic regions now use warning systems and evacuation plans, so that farmers can enjoy the benefits while staying safe.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "Farmers accept the risk in return for larger harvests. ______, the risk is real."
qs.why: 위험을 감수한다는 내용에 대해 위험이 실제라는 대조가 이어지므로 Nonetheless가 알맞아요.

qs.q: What is the function of the sentence "Eruptions can bury fields in a single day"?
o: It explains why the soil is rich
It lists the crops that grow well
It offers a way to avoid the danger
It supports the claim about risk
qs.why: 위험이 실제라는 주장의 근거를 보여 줘요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about farmland far from volcanoes?
o: It cannot grow rice or grapes
It may have less mineral-rich soil
It is always richer than volcanic land
It receives more ash from eruptions
qs.why: 화산재의 미네랄 덕분에 화산 지역의 토양이 비옥하다고 했으므로 먼 지역은 덜 비옥할 수 있어요.

qs.q: The phrase "evacuation plans" refers to plans for ______.
qs.why: evacuation은 위험한 곳에서 안전한 곳으로 대피시키는 것을 뜻해요.

qs.q: According to the passage, what makes volcanic soil rich?
o: Heat that stays in the soil all year long
Minerals from ash mixed into the ground
qs.why: ash that contains minerals ... rain ... mixes it into the ground라고 했어요.

items.title: Late to the Water
items.text: As an adult, I still could not swim, and I had always hidden this from my friends. Last spring I finally signed up for evening lessons at the community pool. The first week was discouraging: I swallowed water, and my legs sank no matter how hard I kicked. The instructor, however, told us that fear was the real obstacle, not strength. Floating on our backs came before everything else. By the fourth week, I could cross the shallow end. Moreover, I discovered that I enjoyed it. Of course, I am still slow; in fact, children in the next lane often pass me. Nevertheless, I no longer feel embarrassed. Learning late has one advantage: nobody expects you to be good, so every small step feels like a victory.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "My legs sank no matter how hard I kicked. The instructor, ______, told us that fear was the real obstacle."
qs.why: 다리가 가라앉는다는 내용에 대해 강사는 다른 관점을 말하므로 however가 알맞아요.

qs.q: What does the sentence beginning "Moreover, I discovered..." do?
o: It contrasts with the earlier progress
It explains why lessons were hard
It gives an example of fear
qs.why: Moreover는 앞의 긍정적 변화에 또 다른 긍정적 사실을 덧붙여요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about why the narrator waited to learn?
o: The community pool had just opened
The narrator had no free evenings
The narrator disliked all water sports
qs.why: always hidden this from my friends와 no longer feel embarrassed에서 창피함 때문에 늦게 시작했음을 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: The word "discouraging" in the passage is closest in meaning to ______.
o: free of any cost to join
qs.why: discouraging은 자신감을 잃게 한다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What did the instructor teach first?
o: How to float on the back
How to hold a breath underwater
qs.why: Floating on our backs came before everything else라고 했어요.

items.title: The Paper Towel Test
items.text:
Lena: Have you picked a topic for the science fair yet?
Omar: Not really. I want to test which paper towel absorbs the most water, but it feels too simple.
Lena: It is simple. However, simple experiments are easier to control, so your results will be more reliable.
Omar: That's true. Still, the judges may prefer something more original.
Lena: Then add a twist. For example, you could test the towels again after they get wet twice, to see which one stays strong.
Omar: Nice idea. In addition, I could make a graph from the data of each trial.
Lena: Exactly. You should start this weekend, because every test needs repeating at least three times.
Omar: Three times? That takes a lot of towels.
Lena: Well, think of it as an investment in a good grade.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "It is simple. ______, simple experiments are easier to control."
qs.why: 단순하다는 말과 대비되는 장점을 말하므로 However가 알맞아요.

qs.q: What is the function of Lena's sentence beginning "For example, you could test the towels again..."?
o: It rejects Omar's original idea completely
It explains why graphs are useful
It warns about the cost of towels
It gives a concrete way to add a twist
qs.why: twist(색다른 요소)를 더하는 구체적인 예를 들어요.

qs.q: What does Omar's last remark suggest?
o: He plans to stop the experiment
He thinks the judges dislike simple topics
He wants to test only once
He is surprised by the number of towels
qs.why: That takes a lot of towels는 필요한 수건의 양에 놀랐다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: The word "twist" in the dialogue is closest in meaning to ______.
o: a careful rule for every test
qs.why: add a twist는 색다른 요소를 더한다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why does Lena suggest starting this weekend?
o: The towels are on sale now
The judges asked for an early report
qs.why: every test needs repeating at least three times라고 했어요.

items.title: Gray Backpack, Green Leaf
items.text:
Clerk: Lost and Found. How can I help you?
Traveler: I left a gray backpack on the 4:15 express this afternoon. Has anyone handed one in?
Clerk: Not yet. However, the train is still on its route, so the crew may find it at the last stop.
Traveler: I hope so. My laptop is inside, and I need it for work tomorrow.
Clerk: In that case, please fill out this form. For example, describe any stickers or marks on the bag.
Traveler: There's a green keychain shaped like a leaf on the zipper.
Clerk: That helps. In addition, leave a phone number so we can call you as soon as it arrives.
Traveler: Of course. Should I wait here?
Clerk: No, it may take a few hours. I suggest going home, and we will contact you tonight.
Traveler: Thank you. I'll keep my phone on.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "Not yet. ______, the train is still on its route, so the crew may find it at the last stop."
qs.why: 아직 접수되지 않았다는 말과 대비되는 희망적인 사실이므로 However가 알맞아요.

qs.q: What does the clerk's "For example" introduce?
o: A reason the train was late
Details to write on the form
A rule about waiting in the station
A list of lost items in the office
qs.why: For example 뒤에 양식에 적을 수 있는 구체적인 정보가 이어져요.

qs.q: What will most likely happen next?
o: The traveler will take the next express train
The clerk will give the traveler a new bag
The traveler will give a number and go home
The traveler will wait at the station overnight
qs.why: 전화번호를 남기고 집에 가 있으라는 안내를 받았으므로 그렇게 할 거예요.

qs.q: The phrase "handed in" is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: handed in은 분실물을 직원에게 제출했다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Which detail will help identify the bag?
o: A sticker of a train on the side
A broken zipper on the pocket
A name tag on the front
qs.why: a green keychain shaped like a leaf on the zipper라고 했어요.

items.title: Saturday Mornings
items.text:
Nadia: I got offered a weekend job at a bakery.
Theo: Congratulations! Are you going to take it?
Nadia: I'm not sure. The pay is decent. However, I'd have to work every Saturday morning.
Theo: That's a lot, since you also have basketball practice then.
Nadia: Right. On the other hand, I want to save money for summer camp.
Theo: Then maybe ask for Sundays instead. For example, many shops need extra help on Sunday afternoons.
Nadia: Good point. In addition, I could ask the manager for fewer hours at first.
Theo: Smart. And if the manager says no, you will at least know how flexible the job is.
Nadia: True. I'll call tomorrow.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "The pay is decent. ______, I'd have to work every Saturday morning."
qs.why: 좋은 급여와 대비되는 단점이 이어지므로 However가 알맞아요.

qs.q: What does Nadia's sentence beginning "On the other hand" do?
o: It gives a reason in favor of the job
It repeats the problem with Saturdays
qs.why: 앞의 단점과 대비되어 일을 하고 싶은 이유(캠프 비용)를 말해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Nadia's Saturday mornings?
o: Nadia usually sleeps late on Saturdays
Nadia works at the bakery already
Nadia has no plans on weekends
qs.why: Theo가 basketball practice가 그때 있다고 말한 데서 이미 정기 활동이 있음을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: The word "decent" in the dialogue is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: The pay is decent는 급여가 꽤 괜찮다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What are the speakers mainly doing?
o: Choosing a gift for a manager
qs.why: 일자리 제안을 받아들일지 따져 보고 시간 조정 방법을 의논하고 있어요.

items.title: Choosing a Phone Plan
items.text:
Clerk: Welcome. Are you looking for a new phone plan?
Customer: Yes. I watch a lot of videos on the bus.
Clerk: Then the unlimited plan fits you. It costs more. However, it never slows down.
Customer: How much more?
Clerk: Fifteen dollars a month. For example, the basic plan is twenty dollars and the unlimited one is thirty-five.
Customer: That is quite a jump. Is there anything in between?
Clerk: Yes. The medium plan has twenty gigabytes. In addition, it lets you share data with a family member.
Customer: Good. Last month I used only fourteen gigabytes, so the medium plan makes sense.
Clerk: Then I'll set it up. You'll receive a text message to confirm.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "It costs more. ______, it never slows down."
qs.why: 비용이 더 든다는 단점에 대비되는 장점이므로 However가 알맞아요.

qs.q: What is the function of the clerk's prices "twenty dollars" and "thirty-five"?
o: They show that the plans have changed
They show how much the plans differ
They explain why the bus is slow
They prove the medium plan is best
qs.why: For example 뒤의 가격들이 15달러 차이를 구체적으로 보여 줘요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the customer's data use?
o: It is above thirty gigabytes a month
It is lower than the basic plan allows
It is below twenty gigabytes a month
qs.why: 지난달 14기가바이트를 썼다고 했으므로 20기가바이트보다 적어요.

qs.q: The phrase "quite a jump" is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: quite a jump는 가격이 크게 오른다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What extra feature does the medium plan include?
o: Faster speed on the bus route
qs.why: it lets you share data with a family member라고 했어요.

items.title: A New Time for Thursday
items.text:
Receptionist: Riverside Clinic, how can I help you?
Patient: I have a checkup at ten on Thursday, but I just learned I have to travel for work.
Receptionist: I see. Unfortunately, Thursday afternoon is full. However, we have openings on Friday morning.
Patient: Friday works, but I must finish before nine. I have a meeting later.
Receptionist: Eight-thirty is available. I'll move your appointment to that time.
Patient: Thank you. Do I need to do anything beforehand?
Receptionist: For example, you should not eat for eight hours before your blood test. In addition, please bring your insurance card.
Patient: Understood. I'll skip breakfast.
Receptionist: Great. We'll send a reminder message tonight.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "Thursday afternoon is full. ______, we have openings on Friday morning."
qs.why: 목요일 오후는 꽉 찼다는 말과 대비되는 가능한 시간이므로 However가 알맞아요.

qs.q: What does "In addition, please bring your insurance card" do?
o: It gives a reason for the delay
qs.why: In addition은 앞의 안내에 또 하나의 안내를 덧붙여요.

qs.q: Why does the patient say, "I'll skip breakfast"?
o: To avoid being late for work today
Because the clinic serves free food
Because of a rule about travel
qs.why: 검사 전 8시간 금식 안내를 듣고 아침을 거르겠다고 한 거예요.

qs.q: The word "openings" in the dialogue is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: openings는 예약 가능한 시간을 뜻해요.

qs.q: Why does the patient call the clinic?
o: To ask about a blood test result
To pay for a clinic visit
To cancel a meeting at work
qs.why: 출장 때문에 목요일 예약을 바꾸려고 전화했어요.

items.title: Online Classes Debate
items.text:
Dana: For our debate, we're arguing that online classes are better. What's our strongest point?
Ravi: Flexibility. Students can learn from anywhere, so nobody loses time traveling to school.
Dana: Good. However, the other team will say that online students feel isolated.
Ravi: Then we need evidence. For example, some schools run online study groups where students chat after lessons.
Dana: That helps. In addition, we could mention that recorded lessons can be replayed before exams.
Ravi: Yes, and that's a big advantage for slow note-takers. Still, we shouldn't pretend there are no problems.
Dana: Agreed. If we admit the weakness first, we sound more honest. So let's prepare a short answer about internet access.
Ravi: I'll draft it tonight and send it to you.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "Online classes save travel time. ______, the other team will say online students feel isolated."
qs.why: 찬성 논거에 대해 상대 팀의 반박이 이어지므로 However가 알맞아요.

qs.q: What is the function of Ravi's example about online study groups?
o: It proves that recordings are useful
It lists several problems with internet access
It shows a possible reply to the objection
It shows that debates are unfair
qs.why: 고립된다는 반론에 대한 대응 근거로 스터디 그룹을 예로 들어요.

qs.q: What does Dana believe about admitting a weakness first?
o: It is not allowed in school debates
It is only useful for the other team
It makes the team seem trustworthy
qs.why: we sound more honest라고 했으므로 신뢰를 높인다고 생각해요.

qs.q: The word "isolated" in the dialogue is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: isolated는 다른 사람들과 단절된 상태를 뜻해요.

qs.q: What will Ravi do tonight?
o: Record a lesson for the exams
Set up a new study group online for the team
Draft an answer about internet access
qs.why: I'll draft it tonight 앞의 'a short answer about internet access'를 가리켜요.

items.title: Train or Bus to the Coast
items.text:
Ines: Our trip to the coast is next month. Should we take the train or the bus?
Paul: The train is faster by almost an hour.
Ines: True. However, it costs twice as much, and we're on a tight budget.
Paul: The bus also stops near the beach. For example, the number 12 leaves us two blocks from the hotel.
Ines: In addition, the seats are wider, so we can sleep a little.
Paul: But the road gets crowded on holidays. Therefore, the bus might take much longer than the schedule says.
Ines: Good point. Is our trip on a holiday weekend?
Paul: No, it's the week after. So traffic should be normal.
Ines: Then let's book the bus.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "The train is faster. ______, it costs twice as much."
qs.why: 기차가 빠르다는 장점과 요금이 두 배라는 단점이 대비되므로 However가 알맞아요.

qs.q: What does "Therefore" show in Paul's warning?
o: A result of crowded roads on holidays
A choice between two hotels near the beach
A reason to take the train
An example of a cheap ticket
qs.why: 휴일에 도로가 붐비는 것이 원인이고 버스가 더 오래 걸릴 수 있다는 것이 결과예요.

qs.q: Why does Ines ask whether the trip is on a holiday weekend?
o: To find a cheaper hotel by the sea
To check if Paul's warning applies
To avoid paying for the train
qs.why: 휴일 교통 혼잡 경고가 이번 여행에 해당하는지 확인하려는 거예요.

qs.q: The phrase "tight budget" is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: tight budget은 쓸 수 있는 돈이 빠듯하다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What do the speakers decide?
qs.why: 마지막에 Then let's book the bus라고 했어요.

items.title: A Book for the Report
items.text:
Student: Excuse me, I need a book for a history report about ancient bridges.
Librarian: We have several. This one is detailed, but it is quite long. Do you have time to read it?
Student: The report is due Friday, so not really.
Librarian: In that case, try this shorter guide. It has fewer pages. Nevertheless, it covers the main designs.
Student: Does it include pictures?
Librarian: Yes, many. For example, there are drawings that show how arches carry weight.
Student: Perfect. I also need a second source. Can I use a website?
Librarian: Sure, as long as it's reliable. In addition, our database has articles from museums. I can show you.
Student: Thanks. Let's do that after I check out this guide.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "It has fewer pages. ______, it covers the main designs."
qs.why: 페이지가 적다는 점과 대비되게 주요 설계를 다루므로 Nevertheless가 알맞아요.

qs.q: What does "In that case" refer to?
o: The guide having many pictures in it
The student having little time before Friday
qs.why: 보고서 마감이 금요일이라 시간이 없다는 상황을 가리켜요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the longer book?
o: It has been taken out by another student
It would take too long to finish
qs.why: detailed하지만 길고 마감이 가까워 읽기 어렵다는 흐름이에요.

qs.q: The word "reliable" in the dialogue is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: reliable source는 믿을 수 있는 자료를 뜻해요.

qs.q: What will the librarian show the student?
o: A list of the most famous bridges
qs.why: our database has articles from museums. I can show you라고 했어요.

items.title: Seeds and Schedules
items.text:
Sofia: The city said we can use the empty lot for a community garden.
Ben: Great! But who will water the plants every day?
Sofia: We could make a schedule. Each family takes one day a week.
Ben: That works. However, some neighbors travel in summer.
Sofia: Then they can swap days. We can also install a rain barrel to collect water, so we won't use much from the tap.
Ben: Smart. What about tools? Shovels and rakes cost a lot.
Sofia: I know. Therefore, I asked the hardware store about donations. They said they would lend us a set for the first season.
Ben: That's generous. Let's plant tomatoes and beans first, since they grow quickly.
Sofia: Agreed. I'll print a sign-up sheet this evening.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "Tools cost a lot. ______, I asked the hardware store about donations."
qs.why: 도구가 비싸다는 것이 원인이고 기부를 문의한 것이 결과이므로 Therefore가 알맞아요.

qs.q: What does Ben's sentence beginning "However" do?
o: It praises the watering schedule highly
It changes the topic to tools
It raises a problem with the schedule
It gives an example of a donation
qs.why: However 뒤에 여름에 여행 가는 이웃이 있어 일정에 문제가 생길 수 있다고 말해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the garden's first season?
o: The volunteers will use borrowed tools
The garden will have no vegetables
The city will water the plants
Every family will buy new rakes
qs.why: 가게가 첫 시즌 동안 도구 한 세트를 빌려 주기로 했어요.

qs.q: The word "swap" in the dialogue is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: swap days는 날짜를 서로 바꾼다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why do they plan to plant tomatoes and beans first?
qs.why: since they grow quickly라고 했어요.

items.title: The Slow Laptop
items.text:
Chen: My laptop has been very slow all week. I can barely open a spreadsheet.
Maya: Have you restarted it recently?
Chen: Not really. I usually just close the lid.
Maya: That may be the problem. A restart clears the memory. However, if it's still slow after that, check the storage space.
Chen: How would that matter?
Maya: When the disk is almost full, the computer struggles. For example, my old laptop slowed down once I stored too many videos.
Chen: I do have hundreds of photos from the conference.
Maya: Then move them to an external drive. In addition, delete programs you never use.
Chen: Okay. As a result, I might not need a new laptop after all.
Maya: Probably not. Try both steps and tell me on Monday.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "I move the photos and delete unused programs. ______, I might not need a new laptop after all."
qs.why: 사진을 옮기고 프로그램을 지우는 행동의 결과이므로 As a result가 알맞아요.

qs.q: Why does Maya mention her old laptop?
o: To suggest buying a new laptop
To support her point about a full disk
To show that restarts never help
To explain how to open a big spreadsheet
qs.why: For example 뒤의 경험이 저장 공간이 차면 느려진다는 주장을 뒷받침해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Chen's laptop?
o: It is far too old to be repaired now
Its storage may be full of photos
qs.why: Chen이 학회에서 찍은 사진이 수백 장이라고 했으므로 저장 공간이 가득 찼을 수 있어요.

qs.q: The word "struggles" in the dialogue is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: the computer struggles는 컴퓨터가 제대로 돌아가지 못한다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: According to Maya, what does a restart do?
qs.why: A restart clears the memory라고 했어요.

items.title: Where to Eat on Friday
items.text:
Tara: We need to pick a place for the team lunch on Friday. Any ideas?
Victor: The noodle place is close and cheap. However, it only has twelve seats.
Tara: There are fourteen of us, so that won't work.
Victor: What about the café with the garden? It has a big patio. Moreover, it's close to the bus stop.
Tara: True. But it rains often this month, so we'd need a backup.
Victor: For example, the patio has a roof over half of it.
Tara: Then let's ask if we can reserve the covered section. Also, Alex is vegetarian, so we need good options.
Victor: I'll check the menu and call them this afternoon.
Tara: Thanks. I'll let everyone know once it's confirmed.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "The noodle place is close and cheap. ______, it only has twelve seats."
qs.why: 가깝고 싸다는 장점에 대비되는 단점이므로 However가 알맞아요.

qs.q: What is the function of Victor's sentence beginning "For example"?
o: It offers a plan for the rain problem
It lists all of the noodle shop's seats
It explains why Alex is vegetarian
qs.why: 비가 올 때를 위한 대비책(지붕 있는 구역)의 예를 들어요.

qs.q: What does Tara's reply "There are fourteen of us" imply about the noodle place?
o: It is too far from the office
It is too small for the group
qs.why: 12석인데 14명이므로 자리가 부족하다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: The word "backup" in the dialogue is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: backup은 대비책을 뜻해요.

qs.q: What are the speakers mainly doing?
o: Writing a menu for a café
qs.why: 인원, 날씨, 식단을 고려해 점심 장소를 정하고 있어요.

items.title: Rescuing the Soup
items.text:
Elena: The soup tastes bland.
Marcus: Did you add salt?
Elena: Yes, a little. Still, it doesn't taste like the one in the recipe photo.
Marcus: Maybe the broth is the issue. Store-bought broth is often weak. For example, homemade broth has much more flavor.
Elena: I don't have time to make broth.
Marcus: Then try adding something sour. A spoonful of lemon juice brightens the flavor. In addition, a pinch of pepper helps.
Elena: Lemon in soup? I'm not sure.
Marcus: Try a small cup first. Otherwise, you might ruin the whole pot.
Elena: Good idea. Oh, that's much better!
Marcus: See? Small changes can make a big difference.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "Try a small cup first. ______, you might ruin the whole pot."
qs.why: 작은 컵으로 먼저 해 보지 않으면 생길 일을 말하므로 Otherwise가 알맞아요.

qs.q: Why does Marcus say "homemade broth has much more flavor"?
o: To suggest buying a lot more salt
To support his point about broth
To say the recipe photo is wrong
To show that Elena has no time
qs.why: For example로 시판 육수가 약하다는 말을 뒷받침해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred from Elena's last reaction?
qs.why: Oh, that's much better!는 맛이 좋아졌다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: The word "bland" in the dialogue is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: bland는 맛이 밋밋하다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does Marcus say will brighten the flavor?
qs.why: A spoonful of lemon juice brightens the flavor라고 했어요.

items.title: Saturday at the Food Bank
items.text:
Grace: Hello, Tomas. I'm calling about Saturday's shift at the food bank. Can you still help?
Tomas: I'd like to, but my cousin's graduation is that morning.
Grace: I understand. However, we're short of people for the sorting table.
Tomas: Could I come in the afternoon instead? The ceremony ends at noon.
Grace: The afternoon shift is full. For example, we already have six sorters, which is our limit.
Tomas: Then maybe I could take a Sunday shift.
Grace: Sunday would be perfect. In addition, we could use someone to drive the van. Do you have a license?
Tomas: Yes. So I could do both sorting and driving.
Grace: Wonderful. I'll put you down for Sunday at nine.
Tomas: Great. See you then.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "Sunday would be perfect. ______, we could use someone to drive the van."
qs.why: 일요일 근무에 더해 운전할 사람도 필요하다는 추가 정보이므로 In addition이 알맞아요.

qs.q: What does the example about six sorters show?
o: Why the sorting table is broken now
Why the afternoon shift cannot take another person
qs.why: 오후 근무는 이미 상한인 6명이 찼다는 사실로 자리가 없음을 보여 줘요.

qs.q: What does Tomas's remark "So I could do both" suggest?
o: He wants to quit sorting at once
He is willing to do more
qs.why: 운전 면허가 있어 분류와 운전을 모두 할 수 있다고 하므로 추가 업무도 맡을 의향이 있어요.

qs.q: The phrase "short of" in the dialogue is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: short of people은 사람이 부족하다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What do the speakers finally agree on?
o: Tomas will work on Saturday afternoon
Tomas will drive the van on Saturday
Tomas will attend the graduation on Sunday
Tomas will work on Sunday at nine
qs.why: I'll put you down for Sunday at nine이라고 했어요.

items.title: Saving for a Bike
items.text:
Nora: I counted my savings. I have forty dollars, but the bike costs two hundred.
Kenji: That will take a long time. How much can you save each week?
Nora: About five dollars. So I'd need nearly eight months.
Kenji: Hmm. Honestly, that is too slow. Could you earn extra money? For example, you could walk the neighbors' dogs.
Nora: I've thought about it. However, I'm allergic to some dogs.
Kenji: Then what about washing cars? In addition, you could sell old books online.
Nora: Selling books is a great idea. I have boxes of them.
Kenji: Even so, don't rush to buy the first bike you see. Compare a few shops.
Nora: I will. Thanks for helping me think.

qs.q: Which connective best fills the blank? "I can save about five dollars a week. ______, I'd need nearly eight months."
qs.why: 주당 저축액 때문에 필요한 기간이 길어진다는 결과이므로 Therefore가 알맞아요.

qs.q: What does Nora's sentence beginning "However" do?
o: It adds a second idea for earning money
It confirms she will walk dogs
qs.why: However 뒤에서 일부 개에게 알레르기가 있어 개 산책 제안을 받아들일 수 없다고 해요.

qs.q: What does Kenji's "Even so" suggest?
o: He thinks the plan is a mistake
He wants Nora to buy a bike now
He plans to sell his own books
He agrees but adds a caution
qs.why: Even so는 계획에 동의하면서도 조심하라고 덧붙일 때 써요.

qs.q: The word "rush" in the dialogue is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: don't rush to buy는 서둘러 사지 말라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why does Nora reject dog walking?
o: She has no time on weekends
She is allergic to some dogs
She already works at a car wash
qs.why: I'm allergic to some dogs라고 했어요.
